summary: zero-baileys 3.3.0: keyword co-occurrence in a WhatsApp library media module without traced installer-harm path
details: zero-baileys is a fork/republication of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. A pattern rule fired on lib/Utils/messages-media.js citing co-occurrence of require("child_process"), https.request(, hostname, and POST across the file. This shape is the ordinary composition of a media-handling module in this library family (ffmpeg/imagemagick invocation for thumbnails/transcoding plus HTTPS media upload/download to the WhatsApp media CDN). No specific installer-side secret read, no environment enumeration, no credential-path access, and no non-first-party exfiltration destination is identifiable in the flagged locations. The library ecosystem has previously shipped covert side-effects using the installer's WhatsApp session (e.g. auto-joining author-controlled channels/newsletters), which is worth a maintainer-side check, but no such behavior is evidenced in the current finding.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
